records antigravity-agent-ux-and-gemini-058, cursor-harness-architecture-093, manus-product-ux-072
corrections: (1) Manus is over-reached. The five-level side-effect map covers only its 22 browser MCP tools. In code it drives only the replay/idempotency action ledger (hasExternalSideEffect -> action key plus digest dedupe) and the MCP annotations. It does not drive approvals or policy. Making 'declared side-effect class drives approval policy' the reference practice is a Verevon synthesis (INF). The closest real references are Hermes (a binary readOnlyHint check, only on servers marked untrusted, asked once per call with no stored allow/ask/never), Claude (a per-tool toolPolicy for its two built-in connectors, with code-defined ask defaults and readOnlyHint skipping) and ChatGPT (DOC, opaque risk tiers). (2) Hermes has a per-SERVER trust tier, not a per-tool allow/ask/never store. (3) In Perplexity, the 'Always allow / Always ask / Never allow' labels appear only in image alt text; the body copy describes Always ask plus once / thread / deny, and recurring runs inheriting thread grants. (4) Claude's never-allow set is 8 tools per BUILT-IN connector (GitHub and Microsoft 365 only), not a general MCP feature. The 'static never-auto set, mode-rank ratchet' is a separate Claude mechanism (claude-extensibility-and-safety-002) and should be labelled that way. (5) The 'per-tool approval policy 3 of 12' figure is inconsistent. antigravity-058 is GitHub per-repository scopes, not per-tool approval. Claude (toolPolicy), Cursor (server:tool allowlist) and ChatGPT (per app and account) do have per-tool or per-app policies but sit in another cluster. Manus team connector 'Requires approval from a team admin' means admin approval to enable a connector, not per-call approval.
